title: Fit a phone's glass screen protector with its alignment tray, from peeling the back film to lifting the empty tray off
instruction: Fit the glass screen protector to the phone with its alignment tray, and leave the empty tray off the phone.
context: Putting a tempered-glass screen protector on a new phone is an everyday job people do at home or watch done at a phone-shop counter. Alignment-tray kits such as Spigen's Glas.tR EZ Fit make it a fixed sequence (Spigen: "Simply place the tray over the phone, press the center and watch the glass adhere in place"; a review: "put the installation tray on the screen after removing the backing tape", "Wait 30 seconds then pull the tab off"): peel back film 1 off by its tab, set the tray level round the phone, press the middle, wait 30 s, peel sticker 2 off by its tab, lift the tray off. Two hands as a person uses them: the film and the sticker are held by adhesive, so a tab pulled with one hand drags the 25 g tray (and the phone) along; one hand holds the tray while the other peels. The tray fits round the phone with 0.4 mm to spare, so it must come down level and square.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. (1) Apple iPhone 16, loose: 14.76 x 7.16 x 0.78 cm, 170 g, switched off, no case, screen wiped clean; screen up, long side along y, top (camera) end toward the left arm; centre x 25.5, y -9.0. (2) Its alignment tray (Spigen Glas.tR EZ Fit kind; sizes estimated), loose, 25 g, clear plastic (drawn grey): outside 7.84 x 15.44 cm plus a flat 3 x 0.6 cm handle at each end; a 4.5 mm skirt that fits round the phone with 0.4 mm to spare a side, 3 mm lead-in chamfer at its bottom inside edge; a seat frame resting on the phone's 1.8 mm black border; a 2 mm deck with a 5.4 x 12.0 cm press window; walls 8 mm tall. It lies skirt down, long side along y, centre x 25.0, y 9.0 (its right-hand end 2.3 cm from the phone's top end), on (3) back film 1: a 0.5 mm sheet under the whole tray with a red pull tab (2.0 x 2.2 cm) standing up 4 mm past the tray's right-hand end, 2.2 cm nearer the robot than the tray's middle. (4) The glass protector, 6.8 x 14.4 cm, 0.5 mm with its films, 7 g (drawn pale blue), held in the tray by (5) sticker 2: an 8 mm yellow strip along the tray's far long edge with a blue pull tab (2.0 x 2.2 cm) standing up 4 mm past its right-hand end. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Events tracked over the run, judged at the end. Film off: film 1 off the tray (sim: its sheet's centre 110 mm or more from the glass's, or 10 mm below it). Seated: tray within 1.5 mm and 2 deg of centred on the phone, resting on it (within 1 mm). Pressed: the glass's middle pressed onto the screen through the window with 5 N or more (PhysX contact force glass-phone; a gripper centre within 20 mm of the glass's centre), tray seated, film off. Sticker off: sticker 2 off the tray (its centre 100 mm or more from the tray's, or 15 mm above it). Waited: the sticker came off 30 s or more after the first press, tray seated. Glass on: flat on the screen (every corner within 0.5 mm of it), every corner within 1.5 mm of its true place along each edge (1.8 mm borders: each border at each corner 0.3 to 3.3 mm), sticker off. Tray off: no part within 10 mm of the phone's outline lower than 20 mm above the screen; hands clear: both gripper centres 30 mm or more from tray, glass and phone; still: all three move under 1 mm in 1 s. 1.0: film off, pressed before the sticker came off, waited, glass on, tray off, hands clear, still. 0.75: the same but the tray still on the phone, hands not clear or not still. 0.5: film off, glass on and pressed, but the sticker came off under 30 s after the press or before it. 0.25: film off only. 0: film still on the tray. Real trial: film and sticker off, the press (a fingertip held on the glass's middle 1 s or more, tray flat on the phone) and the 30 s from the video and its timestamps; borders with a calliper; glass stuck: a photo from above, screen off, a lamp reflected at a low angle, shows no air gap (white, silver or rainbow patch) touching any edge of the glass (bubbles wholly inside the edges do not count).
reset_notes: Each trial uses one kit tray with its glass (the EZ Fit box has two; refill packs are sold). Peel the previous glass off the screen and wipe the screen with the kit's wipe and cloth; put the phone at its taped mark screen up, lay a fresh tray skirt down at its mark with film 1's tab standing at its right-hand end. Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Films are rigid 0.5 mm sheets; each peel is a slide along the tray (25 N s/m drag) that lets go at its end (film 165 mm, sticker 50 mm) to a 2 N pull. The sticker holds the glass on a spring and lets it go at 1.5 N sideways. Adhesion is a rule: pressed glass, let go flat on the screen, stays where it lies. Tray and tab sizes, forces and masses are estimates; the phone's camera plateau is not modelled. Pushing out bubbles and the front film come after.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both arms wandered over the desk; late in the run the left gripper came down over the tray's tab end and nudged the tray, but no tab was taken and the film stayed on); demo: 1.0
